doc: RTAI-003 baseline for crates/anvil-intercept/benches/midedit_roundtrip.rs. Compared against by scripts/check-midedit-baseline.sh during the bench.yml workflow. ADR-031 mid-edit interactive-buffer SLO is the hard-fail gate; this file's per-case p95 is the drift-warn anchor.

calibration.runner_note: Baseline captured on a developer Ubuntu 24.04 / x86_64 box. GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest will produce different numbers — the first CI run on a new runner class will likely emit drift warnings, which are advisory. Re-baseline on the dedicated runner class once CI numbers stabilise. The hard-fail gate (ADR-031 SLO) is runner-independent and remains valid across runner classes.

tolerance.policy: p95 drift outside ±drift_pct is a soft warning (CI passes). The hard-fail trigger is a p95 that exceeds the ADR-031 SLO recorded in .slos for the boundary. p50 and p99 are recorded for context but not gated — see ADR-031 § Regression policy. When a baseline p95 is 0 ms (sub-resolution case) the comparator switches from percentage drift to an absolute floor: a soft warn fires if observed p95 exceeds zero_baseline_floor_ms.

binary_short_circuit.note: Binary short-circuit returns before the rule pipeline runs; sub-microsecond cost is below the wall-clock resolution. With a zero baseline the comparator switches to the absolute-floor mode (.tolerance.zero_baseline_floor_ms): a soft warn fires if observed p95 exceeds the floor. SLO gate (50 ms) still applies.
